subject: Liability cap sequencing — invoice-window floor & recovery multipliers
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA — proposed change to liability cap sequencing

Tessa,

Thanks for the draft MSA. Our legal team reviewed the liability section and asked whether we can (a) anchor the cap to the "fees paid in the prior 12 months" rather than total contract term, and (b) include an explicit offset for any insurance proceeds recovered. The goal is to avoid a situation where a single long-term purchase results in a disproportionate exposure.

Two specific asks from Acme Legal:
- Replace "aggregate liability up to the greater of $X or fees paid" with "liability capped at the greater of $X or amount equal to fees paid during the 12 months preceding the claim."
- Add language that deducts third-party insurance recoveries from any amounts owed under the cap.

They're open to a multiplier (e.g., 2x fees) if we can keep it on a rolling 12-month basis rather than contract-total. Attached is our redline (Acme_Redline_v3.docx) and a simple model (cap_model_v2.xlsx).

Can you confirm whether Redwood has flexibility here and if we need to pull in legal/finance? We'd like to keep the deal timeline but won't accept unconstrained exposure.

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Ellis
Sr. Contract Manager, Acme Analytics
Tom.Ellis@acme-analytics.com

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — proposed change to liability cap sequencing

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks and the model. We can be pragmatic but will need to align with Legal and Finance on the exact mechanics of a rolling 12-month basis and the insurance offset. High level thoughts:

- Rolling 12 months anchored to fees paid is reasonable for commercial customers; we often see both term-wide and rolling approaches depending on revenue recognition patterns.
- Insurance offsets are typical, but we need the right carveout language so it doesn't swallow remediation obligations (e.g., if insurance proceeds are contested or delayed).
- Multipliers (1x vs 2x) materially change exposure — if Acme insists on 2x we may want to combine that with an annual cap (i.e., per-12-month slice) instead of a one-time aggregate.

Looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Sales Ops) to scope the concession and operational implications. I'll work with Legal to propose redline language that preserves commercial predictability.

Next steps: Laura, can you review Acme_Redline_v3.docx and suggest a short alternative that we can send back today? Karthik, can you confirm whether billing patterns for this deal make a rolling-12 approach viable from our revenue/collection perspective?

Tom — we'll aim to get a counterproposal by EOD.

Best,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA — proposed change to liability cap sequencing

Tessa / Karthik —

Quick review of Acme's redline attached. I propose the following compromise language that balances Acme's request with Redwood's need to limit exposure and keep remediation remedies intact:

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Redwood's liability for any claims arising under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) $500,000; or (b) the total Fees paid by Customer to Redwood for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim. For clarity, such liability shall be reduced by any amounts actually recovered by Customer from third-party insurance with respect to the same loss, provided that Customer uses commercially reasonable efforts to pursue such recoveries. This Section shall not limit Redwood's liability for (i) intentional misconduct, (ii) gross negligence, or (iii) indemnity obligations arising from intellectual property infringement claims."

Key points on this draft:
- Anchors to rolling 12 months as requested.
- Includes an insurance offset but conditions it on Customer's reasonable efforts to obtain proceeds (to avoid disputes where they intentionally delay claims).
- Keeps carveouts for willful misconduct/gross negligence/IP — standard.
- If Acme insists on a multiplier (2x), we'd accept as a counter only if the $500k base is reduced (e.g., $250k base with 2x fees) or if we make the cap apply on an annual slice (i.e., per 12-month period).

Karthik — any operational red flags with fees measurement or billing windows? Also flag if Finance needs to confirm the revenue-runway impact of 12-month anchoring.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com; Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA — proposed change to liability cap sequencing

Tom / Team —

Thanks for your patience. We reviewed internally with Finance and Ops. We can accept the rolling-12 formulation with the insurance offset language Laura proposed. A couple of operational notes:

1) Measurement: Fees for the 12-month lookback will be calculated on an invoice basis (gross billed fees), not recognized revenue. We will provide a reconciliation on request during dispute resolution.
2) Multiplier: We are willing to accept a 2x multiplier on the 12-month fees if Acme will agree to a hard annual cap application (i.e., the 2x applies to each rolling 12-month slice and is subject to a per-calendar-year maximum equal to 2x the fees invoiced in that calendar year). If Acme prefers a single aggregate 2x for the entire term, we cannot accept without additional commercial concessions (price or term limits).

If that works, Laura will produce a clean redline and we'll send final language for signature. Tom — would you prefer we put both options in the MSA (rolling-12 default + alt multiplier in the Order Form) so Procurement can sign quickly and legal can pick later?

Marissa is on copy in case we need a commercial tweak for the quote.

Regards,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
